subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — Acme discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>, Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — Acme discovery

Hi Olivia / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can put together a tailored pricing/limits plan: 

1) Usage profile: you mentioned a baseline generation volume and periodic marketing-driven bursts. Can you confirm estimated monthly token volumes (baseline + peak month) and whether embeddings/recency reranking are significant contributors? We attached a sample CSV that would help.

2) Burst behavior: we heard that you get short-duration spikes during campaign launches (hours, not days). Approx peak RPS or tokens/min during those spikes? This matters for rate-limit configurations.

3) Unit economics / budget: you said the finance team is targeting a unit cost target of roughly $/1M tokens. Can you confirm the target band (e.g., <$100 / $100–150 / >$150 per 1M tokens) and any budget range for the next 12 months?

4) Next steps from our side: I'm attaching our rate-limits & overage worksheet (redwood-rate-limits-overage-worksheet.xlsx) — we’ll populate it with your numbers and propose:
   - Recommended quota (committed tokens/month)
   - Burst allowance window and auto-throttle policy
   - Overage tiers and short-burst surcharge rules

If you can send the last 3 months of aggregated token usage (sample CSV is attached: acme-usage-report-may-jul.csv) we’ll model unit economics and return an example P&L showing committed vs. on-demand costs and a recommended committed tier that hits your target $/1M tokens.

Proposed follow-up: 30 min on Thurs 9/10 to review the worksheet — does 11am PT work?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hey Marissa — great call, thanks. Quick answers inline: 

- Monthly tokens: baseline ~300M tokens/month for our recommendation engine + chat support usage. Peak months (product launches) have historically hit ~900M–1.1B tokens/month (for 24–48 hour windows of sustained high traffic across marketing and customer events).

- Bursts: short windows (2–6 hours) where throughput increases ~3x. Peak RPS during those spikes is roughly 12k requests/min across our primary endpoints (generation + chat).

- Embeddings: currently lower volume (approx 50M tokens/month) but growing; embeddings generation is often batched overnight.

- Budget/unit target: finance is leaning toward target <$100 per 1M tokens if we can get predictable committed pricing. They’re willing to consider a reserved 12-month commit if unit economics are attractive.

I uploaded the detailed usage CSV in the thread (attached). Confirm Thurs 9/10 11am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Olivia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme.com>, Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits & overage pricing — Acme discovery

Thanks Olivia — that’s super helpful. I’ve started filling the worksheet with the numbers you sent and sketched two options below. I’ll bring a worked example to the call on Thurs. High level: committed reserved capacity vs. on-demand with overage.

Option A — 12-month reserved (recommended if finance wants <$100 / 1M tokens):
- Commit: 750M tokens/month (covers baseline + typical launch uplift)
- Unit price (committed): $85 / 1M tokens
- Burst allowance: +50% sustained for up to 6 hours/day (auto-throttle after that into queued requests)
- Overage: $120 / 1M tokens after commit is exhausted (billed monthly)
- Short-burst surcharge: if instantaneous RPS exceeds configured burst window (e.g., sustained >200% for >15 mins) an additional 20% surcharge applies to overage tokens in that window.

Example math:
- If month has 900M tokens and you committed 750M: 750M @ $85 = $63,750; 150M overage @ $120 = $18,000; total = $81,750 => effective $/1M ≈ $91.

Option B — On-demand + quota increases (more flexible):
- No commitment; standard on-demand price: $140 / 1M tokens
- Initial quota set to 400M tokens/month with burst allowance (short bursts allowed up to 3x baseline for <4 hours)
- If you exceed quota consistently, you can request quota increase (automated review + 48–72h provisioning) or convert to a committed tier.

We can also structure a hybrid: smaller commit + extra cushion and a lower overage rate.

Next steps for Thurs: 11am PT confirmed. I’ll bring the worksheet populated and an example invoice for both options. Rafael — would you join to talk contract/discount parameters? Camila — please pull the legal/PO checklist we need for a reserved capacity deal.

Best — Marissa
